VVas euer Beard ſo backbitten: this were ynough to make red beards turne medley: and daſh 'hem cleane out of countenance: but I hope like mine they feare no colours: and you were ten Courtiers ile front you: I muſt giue you phyſick with a pox: well, if I pepper ye not, call me Doctor Doddipoll: Maſter Lipſalue and maſter Gudgin you are hartily welcome, I am very glad to ſee you well. Why maſter Lipſalue ? Not ſo ſir, you muſt diſtinguiſh of men: though this J know, vertue is not the end of all ſcience, which commonly keeps the profeſſor poore, ſome ſtudy queſtuary and gainfull Arts, and euery one would thriue in's calling, but yfaith gen tlemen, what wind driues you hither? But not the Stone Collect? If you were troubled with that, my wife can tell you of an excellent remedy. No entreaty gentlemen, you ſhall commaund me to ſearch the very profundity of my ſkill for you. Haue them in wife, and ſhow them their lodging? I will thinke vpon an o ther receipt, and follow you immediatly. To the foole you meane: I know you ha the horne of plenty for me, which you would deriue vnto me, from the li berality of your bawdies, not your minds; here are Lordes, that hauing learnd the O.P.Q. of Courtſhip, trauell vp and down among Cittizens wiues to ſhew their learning, and bringing vppe: as if the City were not already a good proficient in the Court Hornebooke: yes I warrant they haue heads as capa ble as other men; I and ſome of them can wiſely ſay with the philoſopher, that in knowing all they know nothing. VVell, becauſe I am of the Liuery, and pay Scot and Lot a mongſt you, doe but obſerue how ile fetch ouer my gallants for your ſakes; they ſay I am of the right hayre, and indeed they may ſtand too't, and hould the poſition good; ſauing with my wife: ſoft, are they not at pro and contra already? I knowe they are hote ſpurres, and I muſt haue an eye to the maine. They haue bin whipt already for lechery, and yet the pride of the fleſh pricks 'hem; well I muſt in, I haue giuen them ſuch a Pill ſhall take 'hem downe, for luſt muſt haue his fill. O no ſir, vnderſtand me, only father'd vpon me. What elſe ſir, I haue reaſon. Maſter Poppin, you ſhall haue Innocence to ſpeak for me? Then J hope you will be as good to vs, as the fiue-fin ger at Maw. J would giue a hundred pounds my wife had ſo gentle a ſpirit. Here maſter Doctor. You take me wrong maſter Proctor? VVife thou haſt no ſhame nor womanhood in thee, thy conſcience knowes mee. Maſter Doctor I would, were it but to redeeme her loſt good name. That will I inſtantly—So, this is done, which to gether with my Neece doe I deliuer by theſe preſents to the vſe of maſter Gerardine.

By youths: why I tell thee we ſawe Sampſon, and J hope t'is not for youths to play Sampſon : Beleeue it we ſawe Sampſon beare the Towne gates on his necke, from the lower to the vpper ſtage, with that life and admirable accord, that it ſhall neuer be equalled (vnleſſe the whole new liuery of Por ters ſet their ſhoulders) Doe giue and graunt to Maria Glister : Daughter of Iohn Gliſter, and Neece to Docter Gliſter Phyſition, all my leaſes, lands, Chattels, goods and moueables whatſoeuer: This is ſtarke naught, you cannot giue away your moueables, for Miſtris Doctor and Miſtris Purge, claime both ſhares in your moueables by reaſon of their legacies.
She is his Neece. Place it here my honeſt Club, well done: and how does thy miſtriſſe ▪ was ſhe at the Family to day,— ſpit not good Club, J can not abide it. And I pre thee Club what kind of creatures are theſe Familiſts, thou art conuerſant with them. As how good Club ? Not then themſelues Club. Beare your owne? I mary there it goes, what muſt you beare? Your ſins forſooth: confeſſe to me, and goe not a bout the buſh, you haue bin doing thats flat, you haue caught a clap, thats round, and anſwer me roundly to the point, or els ile ſquare. Come whoſe act iſt? I can not deuiſe vnleſſe it be my huſbands, for none elſe had acceſſe to thee; J am ſure time has turnd his bald ſide to thee, and I doe but wonder how thou tookſt oportunity: ſpeake, tell me. VVill you not boult, I muſt ha't out on you, and will. Paſſion of my heart, what art thou? No, but a ſaucy knaue J perceiue by your manners. Whats your name ſir? Orders of knaues, I thought ſo, ſirra y'are a Raſcall to come thus bluntly into my houſe with your durty Star tups, get you without doores like a filthy fellow as you are, a place more fit for you. And whats your buſines heere? From whence? Leaue your ſcraping ſirra: fye how ranck the knaue ſmells of greaſe and Tapſdroppings. VVhat are you Rheumatick too with a vengeance? Did euer ſuch a peaſant defile my floare, or breathe ſo near me: yfayth ſirra you would be bumd for your Roguery if you were well ſeru'd. What an impudent Rogue is this: ſirra be gone I ſay, I would be rid o'you? VVhat's heere Your poore nurſe Thomaſine Sweed leſſe for my life now ſhall I find out my huſbands knauery, I haue ſo long ſuſpected. Tis ſo: Ratsbane: I hate, it rack's on it torments me heere tis, — Woe worth the time that euer I gaue ſucke to a Child that came in at the window god knows how villanous Lea cher; Yet if you did but ſee, how like the little red headed knaue is to his Father damnable Doctor : A Baſtard in the Countrey, and an other towardes here J am out of doubt, this is his wo • ke. You are an Arrant Strumpet, Inceſt, fornication, abomination in my owne houſe; intollerable; O for long nailes to ſcratch out his Eyes. Out of my ſight queane, thou ſhalt to Bridewell —O, I ſhall be mad with rage. Hence you Slaue. The Diuell pay thee. But ile furniſh him ere long if I liue. VVas euer woman ſo mou'd? but you ſhall be talkt withall, and for mine oulde fornicator, he ſhall ha't as hot as coales yfaith: heers ſtuffe indeed! Come mynkes come, ther's Law for you both, haue I found your knauery: if I winke at this, let me be ſtone blind, or ſton'd to death, beare this and beare all. No, thou haſt been all this while in an Vrinall, thou haſt gone out of thy compaſſe in womens waters, Y'are a con iurer (forſooth) and can rouſe your Spirits into Circles, a you old Fornicator that euer I ſaw that read beard of thine; nowe could I raile againſt thy complexion. I think in my conſcience the Traſes & Capariſon of Venus coach, are made o'red hayres which may be a true Embleme, that no flaxen ſtuff, or tan'd white-leather drawes loue like 'hem; J thinke thou manurd'ſt thy Chin with the droppings of Egs and Muſkadine, before it briſled: a ſhame take thee and thy Loadſtone: but tis no mat ter, Maſter Placket the Parritor has cyted you, and you ſhall anſwer it. O I am netled, my patience is ſo prouoak't, that I muſt doffe my modeſty: what ſhall I do? if yee be honeſt gen tlemen, counſell me in my reuenge, teach me what to do, make my Caſe your own. O maſter Lipſalue, I am not the firſt that has ſalne vnder that enſigne: thers no complexion more atractiue in this time for weomen, then gold and red beards: ſuch men are all liuer. True of thy fleſh who knowes not that? thy bearde ſpeakes for thee: I, J, thou lieſt by me like a Stone, but abroade th' art like a ſtone horſe you old Timelifter.
I and to all that forſweare mariage, and can be content with other mens wiues. Maſter Lipſalue, welcome within ken, we two are ſo nearly linkt, that if thou beeſt abſent but one two houres, thy acquaintance growes almoſt mouldy in my memory. And yfaith how yſt: me thinkes thou haſt been a long vagrant. But what newes now? how ſtands the ſtate of things at Bruſſels. VVell fare the City yet: there vertue rides a cockhorſſe cheriſht and kept warme in good ſables, and Fox furre, and with the breath of his noſtrills, driues pride and couetouſnes before him, like's owne ſhaddow: beggers haue whipping cheare, bounty obliges men too't, giues mony for Scrips and Scrolls, & liberality ſeald with ſtrong Armes and Herauldry, to out liue mortality: loue there wil ſee the laſt man borne, ne uer giue ouer while ther's an Arrow i'th Quiuer. She is not ſo ſweet as a potticaries ſhop is ſhe? I, if ſhe would let her Ruffes ſtreame out a little wider; but J am ſure ſhe is ominous to me, ſhe makes ciuill wars and inſurrections in the ſtate of my ſtomach: J had thought to haue bound my ſelf from loue, but hir purging comfets makes me looſe body'd ſtill. Faith ſome Lectuary or ſo. Thou haſt ſounded her then belike. O thats her huſband. Faith friend Lipſalue I perceiue you would faine play with my loue, a pure creature tis, for whom I haue ſought eue ry Angle of my braine: but either ſhe ſcornes Courtiers (as moſt of them doe, becauſe, they are giuen to boaſt of their do ings) or els ſhee's exceeding ſtraight lac't: therefore to preuent this ſmell ſmock, Ile to my friend Doctor Gliſter, (a man ex quiſite in th' Arte magicke) who hath toulde me of many rare experimentes auaylable in this caſe: Farewell friend Lyp ſalue. Maſter Doctor, this my obſcure comming requires an action more obſcure: and in briefe this tis; Sir, you are held a man far ſeene in natures ſecrets, I know you can effect many things almoſt impoſſible; know then I loue miſtriſſe Purge, and oportunity fauours me not, nor indeed is ſhe ſo tractable as I expected, if either by medicine, or your Art magikall, you can worke her to my will, J haue a poore Gallants rewarde ſir. Why by coniuration (I tell you) wherin you are ſaid to be as well practiz'd, as in Phiſick; heer's the beſt part of my preſent ſtore to effect it. Not a man by my Gentry. Of all men liuing, my conuerſation is moſt frequent with Lipſalue the Courtier. I but ſhall your Spirit come arm'd with a whippe too? Is this infallible, haue you ſeen the proofe? Maſter Doctor I would you had ſome ſuite at Court, by the faith of a Courtier, J would beg it for you: Fare you well Sir, I ſhall reporte of you, as I find your charme. O the naked paſtymes of loue, the ſcourge of dulneſſe, the purifier of vncleanneſſe, and the hot houſe of humanity: I haue taken phiſick of maſter Purge, any time this twelue months to purge my humor vpon's wife, & J haue euer found her ſo fugitiue, from exerciſe to exerciſe, and from family to Familie, that I could neuer yet open the cloſe ſtoole of my mind to her: ſo that I may well ſay with Ouid: Hei mihi quod nullus amor eſt medicabilis herbis : now am J driuen to proue the violent vertue coniuration, if it hit, and that I yearke my familiſt out of the Spirit, ile hang vp my Scourge-ſticke for a Trophee, and emparadize my thoughts, though the Doctor goe to the diuell, tis no matter: ha let me ſee; Lipſalues doore open! and himſelfe out of towne? excelle ̄ t Doctor, ſoothſaying Doctor, oraculous Doctor. The apparition: Miſtris Purge peeres through him, I ſee her. Has a no clouen feete, what a laxatiue feuer ſhakes me. My Cue: Clogmathathos. Garragas. Ton tetuphon. What art thou? with the name of Ioue I coniure thee? Tell not me, let me preuent thee, the winde ſhall not take the breath of our groſſe abuſe, we feele the gullery: Ther fore let vs ſweare by our naked truths, & by the hilts of theſe our blades, our fleſh-tamers, to be reueng'd vpon that Parape ropandenticall Doctor, that pocky Doctor. Jf report catch this knauery, we haue loſt our reputati ons for euer, Wherefore lets be ſecret; Ill tax we weomen of Credulity, VVhen men are gulld with ſuch groſſe foppery. COme Boyes, our clothes boyes, and what is the moſt currant newes Periwincle. Muſt we haue no recreation? Why now a ſpeakes like himſelfe, get me a Parritor for her ſtraite? Off boyes, Shrimpe what doſt thou thinke of thy Ma ſter, is a not a rare gull? And Tipple the Tapſter for deflouring a virgin in his ſel ler. Doctor Gliſter, his wife, Maria : miſtreſſe Purge Theſe bee the compleate nomber. Indeed me thinks that ſhould be one end of her thought an't be but to crie quittance with her huſband, or whoſe abuſe the Towne rings. Faith ſince he has ſtrooke with the ſword, ſtrike you with the Scabbard: in plaine termes Cuckold him: you may as eaſilie do't, as lye downe o'your bed. How ſay you to this, is the colour good? do'ſt like you? J, but ſmall hart, and leſſe honeſty. Thats true, for, for one that holds vp his hand at the Seſ ſions, you ſhall haue ten come into the baudy Court. The wind Collect maſter Doctor, or ſome ſuch diſeaſe We need it not, we need it not: but indeed maſter Do ctor, for ſome priuate infirmities (which our waters ſhal make knowne to you) we deſire to take ſome phyſick of you for a few daies, and to that end we would take a lodging in your houſe during the time? And yfaith we ſhall requite your paines to the full. A villanous Doctor. And for my part I haue bin more mortified by her, then euer I was prouokt.
Fellow page, I thinke our acquaintance runs low to, but if it run not o' the lees, lets ſet it a tylt, and giue 'hem ſome dregs to their mouldy flye blowne complements. God ſaue it. In your tother hoſe? ſhe talkt of a ladder of Ropes; if ſhe would let it downe; for my life he would hang himſelfe in't: Jn your tother hoſe? why thoſe hoſe are in Lauender, be ſides, they haue neuer a Codpeece: but indeed there needs no Iuy where the wine is good. In your tother hoſe? This way, that way, ſome way I heard him com ming. Faith there is ſir, but nothing new. Draw ſomewhat neere, and ouer-heare their confe rence?
No rather lets pierce the Rundlets of our running heads and giue 'hem a neate cuppe of wagſhippe, to put downe their Courtſhip. J wonder why many men gird ſo at the Law. Faith ſir, Fortune hath fauoured vs with no newes, but what the Pedlar brought from Norfolke.
Courtſhip, Cartſhip: for the tongues of Complemen ters runne on wheeles: but marke 'hem they ha' not done yet. If his noſe were put i'the remainder of that ſtate Tale, he would ſay twere an vnſauory one. Ile tell thee, becauſe they themſelues haue neither Law nor conſcience. Elſe knocke my head and my pate together, To bring what ſir? ſome more o'your kind. Jle be ſworne ſir, you haue a good looſe, you let fly at chem a pace. VVhy there. I haue heard talke of the Gemini, me thinks that ſhould be a Star fauourable to your proceeding. As if you were ſpit out ons mouth ſir, you muſt needs be like him, for you are both cut out of a peece: but Lord ſir, how you hunt this chaſe of loue, are you not weary? Fattigable (quoth you) you may call it leaneable well ynough, for J am ſure it is able to make a man leane. Loue (ſubbandy luſt) a Punke in this place ſubintelli gitur. Then downe on your knees. Jt dos in deed ſir, like the ſuds of an Alefat, or a waſhing Bole. Maſter, the Doctor the Doctor. You know thats nothing for a new Courtier. No ſir, thats my office, ile run by your ſide. •• ke her councell ſir, get a cullis to your capacity, a re ſtoratiue to your reaſon, and a warming pan to your wit: he comes he comes.
Her Name begins with miſtriſſe Purge dus it not? More is the pitty I ſaye, that fayre weomen ſhould prooue Saintes, before Age had made them croo ked: Tis my lucke to be croft ſtill, but I muſt not giue ouer the chaſe. Vppon my life we are bewitcht, the greaſie Raſ call, that firſt ſeazed Miſtriſſe Purge (by the laſt reflection of the light) appeared to my ſight not much vnlike her huſ band. So is manie a mans beſides yours, and what of that? Ere long hee will take vp his ſtation at a Statio ners, where wee ſhall ſee him doe pennaunce in a Sheete at leaſt.
Not I: I am too ſhallow to ſound her, ſhee's out of my Element, if I ſhew paſſion, and diſcourſe of loue to hir, ſhee tells me I am wide from the right ſcope, ſhe ſayes ſhe has an other Obiect, and aymes at a better Loue then myne. Boy I haue ſpyd my Saint.
speeches.Ma ▪: Let rules of Courtſhip be authentick ſtill, To ſuch as doe purſue variety, But vnto thoſe whoſe modeſt thoughts do tend. To honord Nuptialls, and a regular life As farre from ſhew of niceneſſe, as from that Of impure thoughts, all other obiects ſeeme Reſpectleſſe, of no proportion ballanſt with eſteeme Of what their ſoules affect.
Heer's Club forſooth and his fellowe prentiſe haue brought maſter Gerardines Trunke. Heers a gentleman craues ſpeech with you ſir. He will not tell it me. I can ſee nothing but his eies; the reſt of him is ſo rapt in cloake, that it ſuffers no view. Sir heers another gentleman muffeld too, that deſires preſent conference with you.
Shee's fooliſh ſure, with what imperfect phraſe, And ſhallow wit ſhe anſwers me. VVhom do I ſee? O how my ſences wander? Am not I Hero: art not thou Leander ? Your onely way, go trauell till you tyer, Be rid, and let a gull diſcharge the hyer. Gerardine come forth Maria calls? Thoſe Ribs ſhall not infoulde thy buxom Limbs One minute longer the cincture of myne armes Shall more ſecurely keepe thy ſoule from harmes.
Honeſt Club welcome, is this maſter Gerardines Trunke? he is gone then? Proofe vnaunſwerable maſter Doctor, the Nurſes Letter: let it be red, but firſt obſerue his countenance? it may be his bluſhing will bewray his guilt.
This is logick. But tell me doth ſhe not endeauor to bring my Doctor of her ſide and Fraternity. Faith Mouſe none that I know, more then an old woman that had loſt her Cat, and came to you for a Spell in the recouery. O are you here ſir, I haue brought you a full barne to glut your greedy appetite if you haue any maw, feede here till you choak againe: Now ſhall J ſee the whole Carkas of your knauery ript vp, if thou haſt any grace, now will thy red beard turne white vpon't.
O: haſt thou brought the Trunk honeſt Club, I com mend thy honeſt care, heer's for thy paines. Go in ſweet wife, and giue my Neece good counſel: His name. Shall I vnbutton my ſelfe vnto you; after the receipt of a purgation ▪ for then are their pores moſt open: but what creature of a Courtier is it, hath drawne your head into the woodcocks nooſe. With much facility I aſſure you: but you muſt vn derſtand, that the apparition of a ſpirit is dreadfull, and with all couetous, and with no ſmall ſumme of gold hyred to ſuch feates.
Nothing but commendations, farewell: your ſweet hart Gerardine is by this time cold of his hope to enioy thee: he'es gone, and a more equall and able huſband ſhall my care ere long prouide thee: what clyents haue bin here in my abſence wife? Walke you into that roome, I will bethinke my ſelfe for your good, and inſtantly reſolue you; let the gentle man come in: Lipſalue in loue with my veſſell of eaſe? come to me to helpe him to a morſell moſt affected by mine owne pallat? No more but ſo, I haue ſhapt it, the conceit tickles me. Sir, as a ſtranger J welcome you, what maſter Gudgin haue J caught you: J thought it was a gallant that walkt muffled, Come, let me behoulde you at full, heere are no Sergeants man. So lie thou there; my noble gallants ile ſo firke you: Sir my Spirit agrees in Lipſalues ſhape; to morrow twixt the howres of foure and fiue, ſhall miſtriſſe Purge be rapt with a whirlwind into Lypſalues chamber, thats the fitteſt place: for by the breake of day Lipſalue ſhall be mounted, and forſake the City for three dayes, ſo my Spirit reſolues me ▪ Now ſir, by my Art, at that very houre ſhall his chamber doore fly open, into which boldly enter in this ſort accoutered: put me on a pure cleane ſhirt, leaue off your doublet, (for Spirits indure nothing polluted) take me this whip in your hand, and being entred you ſhall ſee the Spirit in Lipſalues ſhape, in the ſelfe ſame forme that you appeare; ſpeake theſe words here ready written, take three bold ſteps forward, then whippe him ſoundly, who ſtraight vaniſheth and leaues miſtris Purge to your will. And no otherwiſe ſir; let me vnderſtand how you thriue: ha, ha, ha, now to my friend Lipſalue, I muſt poſſeſſe him with the ſame circumſtance, wherein J am aſſured to get per petuall laughter in their follies, and my reuenge. VVhat more flatterers about my carrion? more battery to my walls? ſhall I neuer be rid of theſe Petronell Flaſhes? As for my friend Gerardine, the wind of my rage has blown him to diſcouer countries, and let the ſea purge his loue away and him together, I care not: yong wenches now are all o'the hoigh: we that are gardyans muſt reſpect more beſides Titles, gold lace, perſon, or parts, we muſt haue Lordſhips and mannors, elſewhere as well as in the man: wealth commands all, and wealth ile haue, or elſe my mynion ſhall leade Apes in hell. J muſt after this gallant too, ile know his randiuous, and what company he keeps.

speeches.Mi. Pur,: To the Family maſter Dryfat to our exerciſe.
Nay J will come to you elſe Mayſter Dryfat: thoſe ſenſes (as you terme them) are of much efficacy in carnal mix tures, that is, when we crowde and thruſt a man and a woman together. Do you indeede, bleſſing on your heart: are you vp right in your dealings? I am miſtreſſe Purge, Purges wife the poticarie: what of that?
